summary:
A word can be made by deleting letters exactly when it's a subsequence of `text`. Go through the dictionary
keeping the best word so far (longest, then alphabetically first); run the two-pointer subsequence check only
for words that would beat it. O(D · T) in the worst case, often much less.

question.md:
Return the longest dictionary word that is a subsequence of `text`; ties go to the alphabetically first; if none,
`""`.

- **Up to 1000 words of length ≤ 1000** and text of length ≤ 1000.
- Deleting letters = keeping some letters in order = subsequence.

think.md:
Text `"brazenpanda"`. Hidden words: ['band', 'bread', 'brand']. The longest are five letters; alphabetically, **"brand"** comes first.

The test for each word is the two-pointer subsequence check. The only question is the order of checks: either
sort candidates by the preference and stop at the first success, or scan once and skip words that can't win.

approaches.title: Sort by preference, take the first hidden word
approaches.time: O(D log D · L + D · T)

idea.md: Sort the words by (−length, word). Return the first one that is a subsequence of the text.

notes.c: Sort an array of pointers; the strings stay put.

lines.text: The first hidden word in preference order is the answer.

notes.c: Return a fresh copy, as the caller frees it.

complexity.md: **Time O(D log D · L)** for sorting with string comparisons, plus **O(D · T)** checks in the worst case. **Space O(D)** for the order.

steps.text: 'brand': hidden, so this is the answer.

walk.title: Sort the dictionary by length (longest first), then alphabetically, and return the first word hidden in the text.

limits.md: The sort costs extra string comparisons, and words are reordered just to stop early. A single pass that skips words unable to beat the current best gets the same early cut-offs without sorting.

approaches.title: One pass, check only possible winners

idea.md: Keep `best = ""`. For each word, if it's longer than `best` or the same length and alphabetically smaller, run the subsequence check; on success it becomes `best`.

lines.text: Only a word that would beat the current best needs the (costly) check.

notes.c: Return a fresh copy, as the caller frees it.

complexity.md: **Time O(D · T)** in the worst case (every word checked), often less. **Space O(1).**

steps.text: 'band' would win and is hidden: new best.
'bread' would win and is hidden: new best.
'brand' would win and is hidden: new best.
'zap': can't beat the best, so no check needed.

walk.title: One pass over the dictionary, keeping the best word so far. Only run the subsequence check on words that would beat it.

takeaways.md:
- **"Formed by deleting letters" = subsequence**, checked with two pointers.
- Prune: only test candidates that could improve the answer.
- Spell out the tie-break (length, then alphabetical) and apply it consistently.
